segments.arabic: [1046] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب عن عبد الله بن عامر بن ربيعة أن عامر بن ربيعة أخبره قال:
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amir ibn Rabi‘ah, that ‘Amir ibn Rabi‘ah informed him. He said:

segments.arabic: رأيت رسول الله ﷺ وهو على الراحلة يسبح يومئ برأسه قبل أي وجه توجه ولم يكن رسول الله ﷺ يصنع ذلك في الصلاة المكتوبة
segments.english: I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on his mount, praying voluntary prayers and gesturing with his head, facing whichever direction he turned. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not do this in the obligatory prayer.

segments.arabic: [1047] وقال الليث حدثني يونس عن ابن شهاب قال: قال سالم
segments.english: Al-Layth said: Yunus related to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Salim said:

segments.arabic: كان عبد الله يصلي على دابته من الليل وهو مسافر ما يبالي حيث ما كان وجهه قال ابن عمر وكان رسول الله ﷺ يسبح على الراحلة قبل أي وجه توجه ويوتر عليها غير أنه لا يصلي عليها المكتوبة
segments.english: ‘Abdullah used to pray on his animal at night while travelling, without concern for the direction he faced. Ibn ‘Umar said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray voluntary prayers on his mount, facing whichever direction he turned, and perform Witr on it, except that he did not perform the obligatory prayer on it.

segments.arabic: [1048] حدثنا معاذ بن فضالة قال: حدثنا هشام عن يحيى عن محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن ثوبان قال: حدثني جابر بن عبد الله

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ كان يصلي على راحلته نحو المشرق فإذا أراد أن يصلي المكتوبة نزل فاستقبل القبلة
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray on his mount towards the east. When he wanted to perform the obligatory prayer, he dismounted and faced the qiblah.

notes: The Jabir report retains eastward direction and dismounting/facing the qiblah for obligatory prayer.

segments.arabic: [1049] حدثنا أحمد بن سعيد قال: حدثنا حبان قال: حدثنا همام قال: حدثنا أنس بن سيرين
segments.english: Ahmad ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Habban related to us. He said: Hammam related to us. He said: Anas ibn Sirin related to us:

segments.arabic: استقبلنا أنسا حين قدم من الشام فلقيناه بعين التمر فرأيته يصلي على حمار ووجهه من ذا الجانب يعني عن يسار القبلة فقلت: رأيتك تصلي لغير القبلة، فقال لولا أني رأيت رسول الله ﷺ فعله لم أفعله
segments.english: We went out to meet Anas when he arrived from al-Sham, and we met him at ‘Ayn al-Tamr. I saw him praying on a donkey, with his face towards this side, meaning to the left of the qiblah. I said, “I saw you praying in a direction other than the qiblah.” He said, “Had I not seen the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, do it, I would not have done it.”

segments.arabic: رواه ابن طهمان عن حجاج عن أنس بن سيرين عن أنس رضى الله تعالى عنه عن النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Ibn Tahman related it from Hajjaj, from Anas ibn Sirin, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

comparisons.note: The closing Ibn Tahman route is abridged.

checkedBody: We went to receive Anas bin Malik when he returned from Sham and met him at a place called 'Ain-at-Tamr. I saw him praying riding the donkey, with his face to this direction, i.e. to the left of the Qibla. I said to him, "I have seen you offering the prayer in a direction other than that of the Qibla." He replied, "If I had not seen Allah's Apostle doing it, I would not have done it."

notes: The Ain al-Tamr account retains the donkey, left-of-qiblah clarification and complete closing Ibn Tahman route.

segments.arabic: [1050] حدثنا يحيى بن سليمان قال: حدثني ابن وهب قال: حدثني عمر بن محمد أن حفص بن عاصم حدثه قال
segments.english: Yahya ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to me. He said: ‘Umar ibn Muhammad related to me that Hafs ibn ‘Asim related to him. He said:

segments.arabic: سافر بن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما، فقال صحبت النبي ﷺ فلم أره يسبح في السفر، وقال جل ذكره { لقد كان لكم في رسول الله أسوة حسنة }
segments.english: Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, travelled and said, “I accompanied the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and did not see him pray voluntary prayers while travelling. And He, exalted be His mention, said: ‘There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example.’”

notes: The Hafs account includes the statement about not seeing voluntary prayer and the Quran quotation. Both remain attributed as selected.

The selected Arabic says Ibn Umar travelled; the historical print reads سألت ابن عمر, I asked Ibn Umar. This edition difference remains unresolved; the selected reading and its first-person did not see qualification are retained. The Quran quotation is translated only to its selected endpoint, without inserting a verse number or the remainder of the verse. The divine honorific is retained.

segments.english: I accompanied the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he did not exceed two rak‘ahs while travelling. And Abu Bakr, ‘Umar and ‘Uthman likewise, may Allah Most High be pleased with them.

segments.english: Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Amr, from Ibn Abi Layla, who said:

segments.arabic: ما أنبأنا أحد أنه رأى النبي ﷺ صلى الضحى غير أم هانئ ذكرت أن النبي ﷺ يوم فتح مكة اغتسل في بيتها فصلى ثمان ركعات فما رأيته صلى صلاة أخف منها غير أنه يتم الركوع والسجود
segments.english: No one informed us that he had seen the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray Duha except Umm Hani’. She mentioned that on the day of the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed in her house and prayed eight rak‘ahs: “I never saw him pray a lighter prayer than that, yet he completed the bowing and prostration.”

segments.english: I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when travelling in haste on a journey, delay the Maghrib prayer until he combined it with ‘Isha’.

segments.arabic: قال سالم وكان عبد الله يفعله إذا أعجله السير ويقيم المغرب فيصليها ثلاثا ثم يسلم ثم قلما يلبث حتى يقيم العشاء فيصليها ركعتين ثم يسلم ولا يسبح بينهما بركعة ولا بعد العشاء بسجدة حتى يقوم من جوف الليل
segments.english: Salim said: ‘Abdullah used to do this when travelling in haste. He would say the iqamah for Maghrib and pray it as three rak‘ahs, then say the taslim. Then he would wait only a little before saying the iqamah for ‘Isha’, praying it as two rak‘ahs, then saying the taslim. He would not pray a single voluntary rak‘ah between them, nor a prostration after ‘Isha’, until he rose during the middle of the night.

notes: The full Salim/Ibn Umar report preserves the separate iqamah, three then two units, and the negative clauses about intervening and subsequent voluntary prayer.

Salim’s account remains attributed. Both iqamahs, both taslims, three and two rakahs, the negative intervening-rakah and after-Isha prostration clauses and middle-of-night endpoint remain; the two negative units are not collapsed into one general sentence.

segments.arabic: [1060] حدثنا حسان الواسطي قال: حدثنا المفضل بن فضالة عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب عن أنس بن مالك رضى الله تعالى عنه قال:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ إذا ارتحل قبل أن تزيغ الشمس أخر الظهر إلى وقت العصر ثم يجمع بينهما وإذا زاغت صلى الظهر ثم ركب
segments.english: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, set out before the sun declined, he would delay Dhuhr until the time of ‘Asr, then combine them. If it had declined, he would pray Dhuhr, then mount.

segments.arabic: [1062] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد عن مالك عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها أنها قالت
segments.english: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us, from Malik, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: صلى رسول الله ﷺ في بيته وهو شاك فصلى جالسا وصلى وراءه قوم قياما فأشار إليهم أن اجلسوا فلما انصرف قال إنما جعل الإمام ليؤتم به فإذا ركع فاركعوا وإذا رفع فارفعوا
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed in his house while he was ill. He prayed sitting, while people prayed behind him standing. He gestured to them to sit. When he had finished, he said, “The imam is appointed only to be followed. When he bows, bow; and when he rises, rise.”

segments.arabic: [1063] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: حدثنا ابن عيينة عن الزهري عن أنس رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Ibn ‘Uyaynah related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: سقط رسول الله ﷺ من فرس فخدش أو فجحش شقه الأيمن فدخلنا عليه نعوده فحضرت الصلاة فصلى قاعدا فصلينا قعودا، وقال إنما جعل الإمام ليؤتم به فإذا كبر فكبروا وإذا ركع فاركعوا وإذا رفع فارفعوا وإذا قال سمع الله لمن حمده فقولوا ربنا ولك الحمد
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, fell from a horse, and his right side was scratched, or grazed. We went in to visit him during his illness. The time for prayer came, and he prayed sitting, so we prayed sitting. He said, “The imam is appointed only to be followed. When he says the takbir, say the takbir; when he bows, bow; when he rises, rise; and when he says, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him,’ say, ‘Our Lord, and to You belongs praise.’”

comparisons.note: The locator body includes the first Imran-route fragment belonging to the following digital entry.

checkedBody: Allah's Apostle (p.b.u.h) fell down from a horse and his right side was either injured or scratched, so we went to inquire about his health. The time for the prayer became due and he offered the prayer while sitting and we prayed while standing. He said, "The Imam is to be followed; so if he says Takbir, you should also say Takbir, and if he bows you should also bow; and when he lifts his head you should also do the same and if he says: Sami'a-l-lahu Liman Hamidah (Allah hears whoever sends his praises to Him) you should say: Rabbana walakal-Hamd (O our Lord! All the praises are for You.") (See Hadith No. 656 Vol. 1).

segments.arabic: [1064] حدثنا إسحاق بن منصور قال: أخبرنا روح بن عبادة أخبرنا حسين عن عبد الله بن بريدة عن عمران بن حصين رضى الله تعالى عنه

segments.arabic: أنه سأل نبي الله ﷺ
segments.english: He asked the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

segments.arabic: أخبرنا إسحاق قال: أخبرنا عبد الصمد قال: سمعت أبي قال: حدثنا الحسين عن ابن بريدة قال: حدثني عمران بن حصين

segments.arabic: وكان مبسورا قال: سألت رسول الله ﷺ عن صلاة الرجل قاعدا، فقال إن صلى قائما فهو أفضل ومن صلى قاعدا فله نصف أجر القائم ومن صلى نائما فله نصف أجر القاعد
segments.english: He had hemorrhoids. He said: I asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about a man praying sitting. He said, “If he prays standing, that is better. Whoever prays sitting has half the reward of one who stands, and whoever prays lying down has half the reward of one who sits.”

segments.arabic: [1065] حدثنا أبو معمر قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث قال: حدثنا حسين المعلم عن عبد الله بن بريدة
segments.english: Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: Husayn al-Mu‘allim related to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn Buraydah:

segments.arabic: أن عمران بن حصين وكان رجلا مبسورا، وقال أبو معمر مرة عن عمران قال: سألت النبي ﷺ عن صلاة الرجل وهو قاعد، فقال من صلى قائما فهو أفضل ومن صلى قاعدا فله نصف أجر القائم ومن صلى نائما فله نصف أجر القاعد
segments.english: ‘Imran ibn Husayn, who was a man with hemorrhoids—and Abu Ma‘mar once said, “from ‘Imran”—said: I asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about a man praying while sitting. segments.arabic: [1068] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن عبد الله بن يزيد وأبي النضر مولى عمر بن عبيد الله عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن عائشة أم المؤمنين رضى الله تعالى عنها
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from ‘Abdullah ibn Yazid and Abu al-Nadr, the freedman of ‘Umar ibn ‘Ubayd Allah, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘A’ishah, Mother of the Believers, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ كان يصلي جالسا فيقرأ وهو جالس فإذا بقي من قراءته نحو من ثلاثين أو أربعين آية قام فقرأها وهو قائم ثم يركع ثم سجد يفعل في الركعة الثانية مثل ذلك فإذا قضى صلاته نظر فإن كنت يقظى تحدث معي وإن كنت نائمة اضطجع
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray sitting, reciting while sitting. When about thirty or forty verses remained of his recitation, he would stand and recite them while standing, then bow, then prostrate. He would do the same in the second rak‘ah. When he finished his prayer, he would look: if I was awake, he would talk with me, and if I was asleep, he would lie down.

checkedBody: (the mother of the faithful believers) Allah's Apostle (in his last days) used to pray sitting. He would recite while sitting, and when thirty or forty verses remained from the recitation he would get up and recite them while standing and then he would bow and prostrate. He used to do the same in the second Raka. After finishing the Prayer he used to look at me and if I was awake he would talk to me and if I was asleep, he would lie down.
